Home Remodeling in Bonney Lake, WA

Expert remodeling services for Bonney Lake homeowners — from Lake Tapps to the plateau neighborhoods.

Bonney Lake has been one of the fastest-growing communities in Pierce County, and I’ve watched this city change a lot since I started Pacific Remodeling in 2018. What used to be a quiet plateau community east of Puyallup is now a thriving residential area with thousands of homes that are hitting the age where they need their first real updates. If your house was built in the early 2000s or 2010s, those builder-grade finishes are starting to show their age. I work in Bonney Lake regularly and know this housing stock well.

Bonney Lake Neighborhoods We Serve

Lake Tapps Corridor. The Lake Tapps area is the crown jewel of Bonney Lake living. Homes along the lake range from modest ramblers to larger custom builds, and many of the 1990s and early 2000s homes here are prime for kitchen and bathroom upgrades. I’ve done several kitchen remodels in the Lake Tapps corridor where the homeowners wanted to take advantage of their lake views by opening up the kitchen layout and adding a larger window over the sink. A mid-range kitchen remodel in this area typically runs $39,000 to $88,000.

Fennel Ridge and Fennel Creek Area. The subdivisions along Fennel Creek are packed with homes built between 2000 and 2015. These are mostly 3- and 4-bedroom family homes with standard builder layouts. The kitchens usually have laminate countertops, basic oak or maple cabinets, and linoleum or low-grade tile flooring. I’ve replaced hundreds of square feet of those original surfaces in this neighborhood. A countertop-and-cabinet upgrade here typically costs $23,000 to $56,000.

Sky Island. Sky Island is one of the more established neighborhoods on the plateau. The homes tend to be from the mid-1990s to early 2000s, which means they’ve had time to show their age. Bathrooms with pink or beige tile, vanities with cultured marble tops, and brass fixtures are common. A full bathroom remodel in Sky Island runs $18,000 to $45,000 depending on scope.

Allan Yorke Park Area. The developments near Allan Yorke Park are a mix of newer construction and homes from the mid-2000s. Families with kids make up a big chunk of the homeowner base here, and the projects I do tend to focus on making kitchens more functional for busy households. Think bigger islands, better pantry storage, and durable quartz countertops that can handle daily use.

SR-410 Corridor. The homes along the State Route 410 corridor, especially east toward Buckley, tend to sit on slightly larger lots. Some properties here are on well water rather than city water, which affects plumbing decisions during a remodel. I always check the water source during my initial walk-through because well water can require different fixture choices and filtration considerations.

What Makes Bonney Lake Different

Bonney Lake sits at a higher elevation than Puyallup or Sumner, and that affects construction in ways most homeowners don’t think about. Some homes on the plateau have different foundation configurations to account for the terrain. Water pressure can also vary, especially in homes on well systems. During a bathroom remodel, low water pressure means I need to select fixtures that perform well at lower PSI rather than just picking the prettiest showerhead.

The community here is heavily family-oriented. I see a lot of young families who bought their first home and are now ready to make it their own. They don’t want to move. They want a kitchen that works for family dinners, a bathroom that doesn’t feel like a builder’s afterthought, and quality finishes that will last until the kids are grown.

Cost Expectations for Bonney Lake Remodels

Because so many Bonney Lake homes are newer construction, remodeling costs can actually be more predictable than in older areas like Tacoma or downtown Puyallup. You’re less likely to find surprises behind the walls, knob-and-tube wiring, galvanized pipes, or water-damaged subfloors. That said, I never guarantee a price until I’ve done a proper walk-through.

Kitchen remodels in Bonney Lake typically range from $33,000 to $88,000. Bathroom remodels run $16,000 to $48,000. Countertop-only replacements, where you keep the existing cabinets and just swap the surfaces, start around $5,000 to $13,000 for a standard kitchen.

Growing Community, Growing Demand

Bonney Lake’s population has roughly doubled since the early 2000s. New schools, new shopping, and new restaurants have followed. That growth drives property values up, which makes remodeling a smart financial decision. A well-done kitchen remodel can return 60% to 75% of its cost at resale, and in a hot market like Bonney Lake, that number can be even higher.

I’ve had multiple Bonney Lake clients tell me they considered selling and buying a newer home but realized they could get exactly what they wanted by remodeling for less than the cost of moving. When you factor in closing costs, moving expenses, and the hassle of uprooting your family, a $52,000 kitchen remodel starts looking like a bargain.

Home Remodeling in Sumner, WA

Professional remodeling services for Sumner's charming residential community — quality craftsmanship, local expertise.

Sumner sits just minutes from my home base in Puyallup, and I’ve been working on homes here since I started Pacific Remodeling in 2018. This small city has a character all its own. The tree-lined streets near downtown, the views of the White River valley, and the tight-knit community feel make Sumner one of those places where people buy a house and stay for decades. When homeowners here decide to remodel, they’re investing in a home they plan to keep, and I respect that.

Sumner’s Neighborhoods and Housing Stock

Downtown Sumner and Main Street. The homes near Main Street are some of the oldest in the area, with many dating back to the 1920s through 1950s. These houses have personality, but they also have aging plumbing, outdated electrical, and kitchens that were designed for a different era. I’ve remodeled several kitchens in downtown Sumner where the original galvanized plumbing had to be replaced before we could even think about installing new fixtures. A kitchen remodel in an older downtown home typically runs $39,000 to $96,000 because of the additional work required to bring infrastructure up to current code.

The historic Main Street area gives Sumner its small-town appeal. Homeowners near downtown appreciate quality work that respects the character of their homes while making them functional for modern living. That’s exactly how I approach these projects.

East Sumner Developments. Head east of downtown toward Bonney Lake, and the housing stock changes dramatically. The neighborhoods out here feature homes built in the 1990s and 2000s, many of them split-level or two-story designs with standard builder finishes. These homes are in great structural shape but are ready for cosmetic upgrades. I see a lot of homeowners in east Sumner replacing laminate countertops with quartz, swapping out dated cabinets, and converting old tub-shower combos into walk-in showers.

White River Valley Properties. Some Sumner homes sit near the White River flood plain. If your property is in a FEMA-designated flood zone, that affects what kind of work we can do and how we approach it. I always check flood plain maps during the estimate phase. For homes in these areas, we sometimes need to account for moisture-resistant materials in lower-level bathrooms and make sure any plumbing work meets specific requirements. It doesn’t mean we can’t do the project. It just means we plan for it upfront rather than dealing with surprises later.

Why Sumner Homeowners Remodel

Sumner is a bridge community between Puyallup and Bonney Lake, with SR-410 running from Sumner southeast toward the plateau. Families move here because the homes are more affordable than Puyallup’s South Hill or Bonney Lake’s Lake Tapps neighborhoods, but they still get great schools through the Sumner-Bonney Lake School District and safe streets. Once they settle in, they start thinking about making the house their own.

The most common request I get from Sumner homeowners is a kitchen remodel. It’s almost always the same story: the kitchen felt fine when they moved in, but after a few years of living in it, they realize the layout doesn’t work. The counters are too small, there’s no island, the lighting is dim, and the cabinets are wearing out. A well-planned kitchen renovation can fix all of that in 4 to 8 weeks.

Bathroom remodels are the second most popular request. I’ve done a lot of master bathroom upgrades in Sumner where the homeowner wanted to ditch the old builder-grade tub-shower combo and replace it with a tiled walk-in shower. That single change costs between $13,000 and $29,000 and completely transforms how the bathroom looks and functions.

Cost Ranges for Sumner Remodels

Sumner’s housing prices are moderate compared to nearby communities, and remodeling costs reflect that. A mid-range kitchen remodel here typically costs $33,000 to $80,000. A full bathroom renovation runs $16,000 to $45,000. Countertop-only replacements start around $4,500 to $11,000 for a standard kitchen layout.

For older homes near downtown, expect to budget an extra 10% to 20% for the unexpected. I’ve opened up walls in 1940s Sumner homes and found everything from knob-and-tube wiring to makeshift plumbing repairs that previous owners never addressed. My experience working on older homes means I know how to handle these situations without blowing your budget.

The Small-Town Advantage

One thing I appreciate about working in Sumner is that neighbors talk to each other. When I finish a kitchen remodel on one street, the homeowner’s neighbor often calls me within a few months. That kind of word-of-mouth referral is the backbone of my business. I’ve done multiple projects on the same block in Sumner because homeowners see the quality of our work firsthand and want the same for their home.

Sumner’s small-town feel also means the permitting process is straightforward. The city handles its own building permits, and the process is typically faster than dealing with larger municipalities. I take care of all permit applications and inspections, so you don’t have to worry about the paperwork.

Home Remodeling in Edgewood, WA

Expert kitchen and bathroom remodeling for Edgewood homeowners — local knowledge, quality results.

Edgewood has a feel that sets it apart from the rest of Pierce County. Bigger lots, more space between houses, and a semi-rural atmosphere that gives you breathing room without being far from everything. I’ve been working on homes in Edgewood since I started Pacific Remodeling, and the projects here tend to be some of my most rewarding. Edgewood homeowners know what they want, they invest in quality, and they’re building spaces they plan to enjoy for years.

Edgewood’s Character and Housing Stock

Edgewood was incorporated as a city in 1996, but many of the homes here were built well before that. The housing stock is primarily a mix of 1980s through early 2000s construction, with some newer builds scattered throughout. Most homes sit on lots of a half-acre or larger, which means the houses themselves tend to be bigger than what you find in Puyallup or Sumner. More square footage means larger kitchens, bigger bathrooms, and more scope when it comes to remodeling.

The 1980s homes in Edgewood often have those classic dated features: oak cabinets with cathedral-style doors, tile countertops with grout lines that trap everything, brass fixtures, and pink or seafoam bathroom tile. If that describes your house, you’re in good company. I’ve updated dozens of these homes.

Homes from the 1990s and 2000s tend to be in better cosmetic shape but still have builder-grade finishes that wear out. Laminate countertops, hollow-core cabinet doors, and basic chrome fixtures are the norm. These homes are great candidates for a mid-range remodel that makes a big visual impact.

Edgewood Neighborhoods We Serve

Near Surprise Lake. The homes along the Edgewood-Milton border near Surprise Lake are some of the most desirable in the area. Properties here tend to be on larger lots with mature trees and a real sense of privacy. I’ve done kitchen remodels in this area where the homeowner wanted to take advantage of the wooded views by enlarging windows and opening up the kitchen layout. A typical kitchen remodel near Surprise Lake runs $45,000 to $105,000, reflecting the larger room sizes and higher-end finish selections that homeowners in this area prefer.

Jovita Area. Jovita is one of the older parts of Edgewood, and homes here range from 1960s ranchers to 1990s two-story builds. The older homes sometimes need plumbing and electrical updates before cosmetic work can begin. I always check the age and condition of these systems during my initial walk-through. The 1990s homes in Jovita are more straightforward, usually just needing updated surfaces and fixtures.

Along Meridian Avenue. The Meridian corridor runs through the heart of Edgewood, and homes along this stretch are convenient to shopping and schools. These tend to be 1980s to 2000s construction with standard suburban layouts. Kitchen and bathroom remodels here fall in the typical Pierce County range of $33,000 to $88,000 for kitchens and $16,000 to $48,000 for bathrooms.

Why Edgewood Projects Tend to Be Bigger

Edgewood homeowners tend to go bigger on their remodels. That’s not a sales pitch. It’s just what I’ve observed over the years. The larger lot sizes and home footprints mean kitchens are often 150 to 250 square feet rather than the 100- to 150-square-foot kitchens I see in Puyallup’s older neighborhoods. More square footage means more cabinets, more countertop surface, and more flooring. It also means the projects take a bit longer, typically 6 to 10 weeks for a full kitchen renovation.

Master bathrooms in Edgewood homes are also larger than average. I’ve done master bath remodels here with separate shower and tub areas, double vanities stretching 8 feet or more, and dedicated linen closets that we rebuilt from scratch. These projects run $33,000 to $72,000 depending on material selections.

The other thing about Edgewood is that homeowners here tend to choose higher-end finishes. I install more natural stone countertops, custom cabinetry, and premium tile in Edgewood than in any other city I serve. People out here are investing in quality because they’re planning to stay in their homes long-term.

Permitting in Edgewood

Edgewood handles its own building permits through the city’s Community and Economic Development department. The permitting process is generally efficient, and I’ve built good relationships with the staff there. For most kitchen and bathroom remodels involving plumbing or electrical changes, you’ll need a permit. I handle the entire permit process, from application through final inspection, so you don’t need to take time off work to deal with the city.

One thing worth noting: some Edgewood properties are on septic systems rather than city sewer. If your home is on septic and we’re adding a bathroom or significantly changing plumbing layouts, that can affect the septic system and may require additional review. I check this during the estimate so there are no surprises.

My Approach to Edgewood Remodeling

I treat every Edgewood project like I’m building it for my own home. These are well-built houses in a community where people take pride in their properties. When a homeowner invests $65,000 or more in a kitchen remodel, they deserve work that will look just as good in 15 years as it does on day one. That means proper prep work, quality materials, and attention to the details that separate professional work from a hack job.

My background as a third-generation carpenter shows in how I handle the structural side of these projects. When we open up a wall for an expanded kitchen, I make sure the beam work is right. When we install heavy stone countertops, I verify the cabinets and supports can handle the weight. These are the things you don’t see in the finished product, but they’re what makes the difference between a remodel that lasts and one that doesn’t.

Home Remodeling in South Hill, WA

Quality remodeling services for South Hill's growing residential community — from Meridian Avenue to the Sunrise developments.

South Hill is one of the premier residential areas in Pierce County, and it’s one of the neighborhoods I work in most often. I’ve been remodeling kitchens and bathrooms on South Hill since I started Pacific Remodeling in 2018, and the demand here never slows down. Families invest in South Hill homes because of the schools, the shopping, and the quality of the neighborhoods. When they’re ready to upgrade from builder-grade finishes to something that matches how they actually live, they call me.

South Hill Neighborhoods We Serve

Sunrise Village Area. The subdivisions around Sunrise Village are some of the most active neighborhoods for remodeling on South Hill. Homes here were mostly built in the late 1990s and 2000s, and they’re right in the sweet spot for upgrades. The original kitchens came with laminate countertops, basic maple or oak cabinets, and linoleum or entry-level tile flooring. After 20 to 25 years of family use, those materials are worn out. I’ve done dozens of kitchen remodels within a few miles of Sunrise Village, and the most popular upgrade is replacing the entire kitchen surface package: quartz countertops, soft-close shaker cabinets, and luxury vinyl plank or tile flooring. That combination typically runs $36,000 to $77,000.

Meridian Corridor. Meridian Avenue is the spine of South Hill, and the neighborhoods on both sides of it are packed with homes from the 1990s and early 2000s. These are mostly two-story and split-level designs with 3 to 4 bedrooms, built for families. The kitchens tend to be decent-sized but feel dated. I’ve opened up more than a few of these by removing the wall between the kitchen and dining room and installing a structural beam. That one change adds both visual space and functional countertop area. With a 12- to 14-foot LVL beam, you can span most of these openings without any posts.

Canyon Road Area. The Canyon Road side of South Hill has a mix of housing ages, from the 1980s up through brand-new construction. The older homes along Canyon Road need more work, sometimes including plumbing and electrical updates, while the newer homes just need surface-level upgrades. I’ve worked on homes at both ends of that spectrum in this area.

Newer Luxury Builds. South Hill has seen significant new construction over the past 10 years, including some higher-end developments with homes in the $600,000 to $900,000 range. Even brand-new homes sometimes need work. I’ve had homeowners call me within the first year of owning a new build because the builder used cheap countertops, the cabinet hardware was already failing, or the master bathroom tile was poorly installed. New doesn’t always mean well-built.

The Builder-Grade to Custom Upgrade

This is the single most common project I do on South Hill: taking a builder-grade kitchen and turning it into something custom. Here’s what that typically looks like.

The existing kitchen has 30-inch upper cabinets that stop a foot below the ceiling, creating a dust shelf that collects clutter. The countertops are laminate or low-grade granite with a basic edge profile. The backsplash is a single row of 4x4 tiles, or sometimes nothing at all. The lighting is a single fluorescent fixture in the center of the ceiling.

My upgrade replaces all of that. I install 42-inch upper cabinets that reach the ceiling, eliminating the dust shelf and adding 30% more storage. The countertops go to quartz with a polished or leathered finish. We add a full tile backsplash from counter to cabinet. And the lighting gets a complete overhaul with recessed cans, under-cabinet LED strips, and pendant lights over the island. The total investment for this kind of project runs $39,000 to $88,000, and it changes the entire feel of the home.

Why Families Invest in South Hill Homes

South Hill is a popular choice for families in Pierce County. The Puyallup School District serves most of South Hill, and the schools here are a major draw for families relocating to the area. When you’ve got kids in a great school district and you like your neighborhood, selling and moving doesn’t make sense. Remodeling does.

I hear this from South Hill homeowners all the time: “We love this neighborhood, we just don’t love our kitchen.” That’s exactly the kind of problem I solve. For $39,000 to $80,000, you can have a kitchen that makes you excited to cook dinner instead of dreading it. For $20,000 to $48,000, you can have a master bathroom that feels like a retreat instead of an afterthought.

Property values on South Hill have appreciated steadily over the past decade. A well-executed kitchen remodel adds real value to your home, both in appraisal terms and in daily quality of life. I’ve had multiple clients tell me their remodeled kitchen is what sealed the deal when they sold their home years later.

What South Hill Remodels Cost

Here are the ranges I see most often for South Hill projects:

Kitchen remodels: $33,000 to $88,000 for a full renovation, $16,000 to $32,000 for a countertop-and-cabinet refresh
Bathroom remodels: $16,000 to $56,000 for a full bathroom, $10,000 to $24,000 for a tub-to-shower conversion
Countertop replacement only: $4,500 to $13,000 for a standard kitchen
Open-concept conversion (wall removal with beam): $10,000 to $24,000 in addition to the kitchen remodel cost

These numbers are based on projects I’ve actually completed on South Hill. Every home is different, so the best way to get an accurate price is to schedule a free estimate.

Permitting on South Hill

South Hill is an unincorporated area of Pierce County, so building permits go through Pierce County Planning and Public Works rather than a city building department. I handle all permit applications and inspections for my South Hill projects. The county inspection process typically adds about a week to the project timeline, and I build that into every schedule so there are no delays on your end.

My Commitment to South Hill Homeowners

I live near South Hill. I shop at the same stores, eat at the same restaurants, and drive the same streets as my clients. When I finish a project on South Hill, I know I might run into that homeowner at the grocery store next week. That keeps me honest and makes sure every project gets my full attention.

My background as a third-generation carpenter means I understand the structural side of remodeling, not just the cosmetic side. When we remove a wall, the beam work is engineered properly. When we install heavy stone countertops, the cabinet boxes are reinforced to handle the weight. These details matter, and they’re what separates a remodel that lasts 20 years from one that starts showing problems in 5.

Home Remodeling in Orting, WA

Quality remodeling for Orting Valley homeowners, from kitchen renovations to bathroom upgrades.

Orting is one of those communities that doesn’t get enough credit. Tucked into the valley between the Carbon and Puyallup Rivers, this small city has a lot of heart. I’ve been driving through Orting since before I started Pacific Remodeling in 2018, and I’ve watched it grow from a quiet farming town into a community with new subdivisions, young families, and homeowners who are ready to make their houses feel like home. It’s only about 15 minutes from my base in Puyallup, and I work here regularly. The housing stock in Orting is hitting that sweet spot where the older homes near downtown need updates and the newer builds on the edges are ready for their first round of upgrades beyond builder-grade finishes.

Orting Neighborhoods We Serve

Downtown and Historic Core. The homes closest to Orting’s downtown stretch along the original streets near Calistoga Park and the old town center. Many of these houses date from the 1950s through the 1980s, and they come with the typical issues I see in older PNW homes: galvanized plumbing, outdated electrical panels, and kitchens that were designed for a different era. I’ve opened up walls in downtown Orting houses and found water damage behind the sink, old wiring that needed replacing, and subfloors that had to come out before new tile could go down. These homes have good bones, but they need work. A full kitchen remodel in this part of town typically runs $32,000 to $78,000, depending on how much infrastructure work is hiding behind the walls.

Whitehawk. The Whitehawk neighborhood sits on the northwest side of Orting, close to Gratzer Sports Park and the Foothills Trail. Homes here are mostly from the 2000s and 2010s, built during the development boom that reshaped the edges of Orting. These are 3- and 4-bedroom family homes with builder-grade cabinets, laminate countertops, and basic vinyl flooring. Solid houses, but after 15 or 20 years the finishes start to look tired. I’ve done several countertop and cabinet upgrades in Whitehawk. A countertop replacement here costs $4,200 to $11,500 for a typical kitchen layout.

Bridgewater and Newer Subdivisions. Bridgewater is one of the newest communities in Orting, located near Calistoga Way on the northwest side of town. KB Home opened this community in 2025, joining other builders who have been active across Orting’s newer developments. These homes are structurally sound and energy-efficient, but the kitchens and bathrooms use standard production finishes. Homeowners in these subdivisions often call me when they want to swap out the laminate for quartz countertops, upgrade cabinet hardware, or convert a tub-shower combo into a walk-in shower. A tub-to-shower conversion here typically costs $12,500 to $27,000.

Carbon River Corridor Properties. Some of the most scenic properties in Orting sit along or near the Carbon River on the east side of town. Homes here range from 1970s ramblers to newer custom builds. The lots tend to be larger, and the proximity to the river means moisture management is always a factor. I check crawl spaces and subfloors carefully during every estimate in this area, because water intrusion from the high water table can affect what materials and methods I use during a bathroom or kitchen remodel.

What Makes Orting Different

Orting sits in a valley floor between two rivers. That geography matters for remodeling. Moisture is a constant factor. The Pacific Northwest already gets plenty of rain, but homes in the Orting Valley deal with higher groundwater levels than plateau communities like Bonney Lake or South Hill. I’ve pulled up bathroom flooring in Orting homes and found moisture damage in the subfloor that the homeowner had no idea about. My approach is to check for these issues upfront during the estimate walk-through, not after the project is already underway.

The other thing people know about Orting is the lahar zone. The entire city sits on ancient lahar deposits from Mount Rainier, and the USGS has designated it as one of the most at-risk communities in the event of volcanic mudflow activity. Orting has a siren system and evacuation routes in place, and residents here are familiar with the reality. From a remodeling standpoint, it doesn’t change how I build or what materials I use. But it does affect property values and what homeowners are willing to invest. My honest advice: if you plan to stay in your home for the next 5 to 10 years, a well-done remodel is still a smart investment that makes your daily life better.

The Foothills Trail runs right through Orting, connecting the town to South Prairie, Buckley, and Puyallup. It’s one of the best paved trail systems in Pierce County, and homes near the trail tend to hold their value well.

Cost Expectations for Orting Remodels

Orting’s median home prices are lower than neighboring Bonney Lake or Puyallup, and remodeling budgets here tend to reflect that. Homeowners in Orting are practical, budget-conscious, and want quality work at a fair price. That’s exactly how I operate.

Kitchen remodels in Orting typically range from $30,000 to $78,000. Bathroom remodels run $15,000 to $42,000. Countertop-only replacements start around $4,200 to $11,500. Tub-to-shower conversions cost $12,500 to $27,000.

For the older homes near downtown, I recommend budgeting an extra 10% to 15% for surprises behind the walls. Homes built before 1980 almost always have something that needs attention once demo begins. My 20-plus years in the trades means I know how to handle those surprises without derailing your budget or timeline.

Home Remodeling in Buckley, WA

Professional kitchen and bathroom remodeling for Buckley homeowners at the foothills of Mount Rainier.

Buckley sits right where the foothills start getting serious. This small city at the base of the Cascades has a feel that’s different from the rest of Pierce County. It’s quieter, more spread out, and surrounded by trees and farmland with Mount Rainier filling the skyline on a clear day. I’ve been working on homes in the Buckley area since I started Pacific Remodeling in 2018, usually coming out from my base in Puyallup along the SR-410 corridor. The drive takes about 25 minutes, and I make it regularly. Buckley homeowners have a strong sense of community pride, and when they invest in a remodel, they want it done right. That’s exactly my approach.

Buckley Neighborhoods We Serve

Downtown Buckley and Main Street. The oldest homes in Buckley are clustered near Main Street and the original town grid. Some of these date back to the early 1900s, when Buckley was a logging and railroad town. These houses have real character, but they also come with the challenges I see in any older PNW construction: outdated plumbing, small kitchens designed for a different era, and bathrooms that haven’t been touched in decades. I’ve remodeled kitchens in downtown Buckley where the original galvanized pipes had to come out before we could install a new sink. A kitchen remodel in an older downtown home runs $35,000 to $82,000 because of the additional infrastructure work.

Cascade Trails and Copperwynd. These neighborhoods on the west side of Buckley feature homes from the 2000s and 2010s. The houses are mostly 3- and 4-bedroom family homes with standard builder finishes, similar to what I see in newer parts of Bonney Lake and Orting. Laminate countertops, basic cabinets, and vinyl flooring are the norm. After 15 to 20 years, these finishes wear out. A countertop replacement with quartz in these neighborhoods costs $4,500 to $12,000 depending on the kitchen size.

Finlandia and Hamilton Estates. These areas feature wider and deeper lots, giving the homes more of a rural feel even though they’re still within city limits. Properties here are a mix of 1980s and 1990s construction with some newer infill. The larger lot sizes mean the homes themselves tend to be bigger, and the kitchens and bathrooms have more square footage to work with. Master bathroom remodels in these neighborhoods run $16,000 to $44,000.

Enclave at White River and New Construction. KB Home opened the Enclave at White River community in Buckley in 2025, with new homes priced from the $580,000s. This kind of development is changing the look of Buckley’s eastern edge. While these brand-new homes don’t need remodeling yet, the homeowners in the surrounding established neighborhoods are seeing their property values rise. That makes a $45,000 kitchen remodel a smart investment, not just for daily enjoyment but for long-term home value.

What Makes Buckley Different

Buckley is the gateway to Mount Rainier via SR-410. That means this city gets tourist traffic every summer, but the year-round residents are the ones who make the community. The annual Buckley Log Show in June is a reminder of the city’s roots in timber and logging. It’s a place where people know their neighbors and take pride in their properties.

The housing stock in Buckley is more varied than what I see in planned communities like South Hill or Lake Tapps. You’ll find early 1900s Craftsman-style homes a few blocks from 2020s new construction. Farm properties on multi-acre lots sit alongside suburban subdivisions. That variety means every project is different, and I adjust my approach based on what I find during the walk-through.

The White River runs along Buckley’s southern edge, and the Foothills Trail now stretches 22 uninterrupted miles from Puyallup through Orting and Buckley to Enumclaw, thanks to the new White River pedestrian bridge completed in 2024. Homes near the trail and river corridor deal with the same moisture issues I see throughout Pierce County. I always check subfloors, crawl spaces, and window surrounds during my estimate because water damage in the PNW is a when, not an if.

One thing I appreciate about Buckley is the pace. Projects here don’t have the same permitting bottlenecks I sometimes run into in larger cities. The city staff are approachable, and I handle the entire permit process on your behalf.

Cost Expectations for Buckley Remodels

Buckley’s median home price sits around $650,000, which puts it in a moderate range for Pierce County. Remodeling costs here reflect that middle ground between the higher-end Bonney Lake market and the more modest budgets in Orting.

Kitchen remodels in Buckley typically range from $33,000 to $82,000. Bathroom remodels run $16,000 to $44,000. Countertop-only replacements cost $4,500 to $12,000. Tub-to-shower conversions run $13,000 to $28,000.

For older homes near downtown, budget an extra 10% to 15% for the unexpected. I’ve opened walls in 1940s Buckley homes and found everything from knob-and-tube wiring to plumbing repairs held together with tape. My experience means I handle these discoveries without panic and without blowing your budget.
